title: berlin says no intervention needed fill gas storage sites 2026 09 08
text:
BERLIN, Sept 8 (Reuters) - No government intervention is needed to raise German gas storage levels, the economy ​ministry said in a document prepared for a ‌parliament committee meeting, after a lobby group warned of shortages if the coming winter is extremely cold.
"Based on the current volume-based assessment, ​storage levels in the range of 60% to ​70% at the start of winter, together with ⁠further import options, will be sufficient to meet ​the expected winter demand," the ministry said in the ​document for the economic affairs committee, which was due to hold a special meeting on Tuesday evening.
The ministry added that there is ​a price and volatility risk if elevated prices ​persist in the wake of the Iran war. "This must be distinguished ‌from ⁠a physical gas shortage," said the document seen by Reuters.
The ministry also pointed to imports via pipelines as well as liquefied natural gas terminals - an option Germany ​did not have ​during its ⁠2022 energy crisis.
As of September 1, underground gas caverns in Germany were 53% full, ​the lowest in 15 years of records, ​lobby ⁠group INES said.
Energy companies and traders usually store gas during the summer, when prices are lower, but the Iran ⁠war ​has driven up prices, making the ​storing less lucrative compared to selling it on the market.
